practitioners' expectations are not met by current fault localization techniques.

practitioners expect fault localization techniques to be accurate, fast, and easy to use, but they are not willing to pay a price for accuracy and speed if the techniques require significant learning and/or are not easy to use.

The main takeaway from our work is that

practitioners are willing to adopt automated fault localization techniques, if they have the following properties: (1) they do not require a lot of effort to use, (2) they do not need a lot of effort for training, (3) they are easy to understand, (4) they are accurate, (5) they are efficient, (6) they are portable, and (7) they are flexible.
